title: Pro-Life Group Plans Protest Against Cardinal Cupich Over Award in Chicago

tea.why: Pro-life groups object to the Archdiocese of Chicago honoring a philanthropist who has donated to Planned Parenthood and reproductive funds.
tea.want: Protesters demanded that the Archdiocese cancel or halt its recognition of the award recipient.
tea.changed: Oct 29: Illinois Right to Life staged a public protest at the Archdiocese of Chicago's Rerum Novarum Banquet.

summary: Pro-life activists announced plans to publicly protest the Archdiocese of Chicago's Rerum Novarum Banquet in Chicago, Illinois. Organised by Illinois Right to Life, the protest aimed to object to Cardinal Blase Cupich presenting the Nostra Aetate Award to billionaire businessman and philanthropist Michael Sacks. According to sources, Sacks has donated substantial funds to organizations supporting abortion access, including Planned Parenthood of Illinois and the Prairie State Access Fund. Illinois Right to Life accused Cardinal Cupich of scandalizing the faithful by bestowing the honor. In response, Cardinal Cupich stated that the award recognizes the recipient's community leadership and generosity within the Jewish community, and does not imply an endorsement of every stance or statement held by the recipient.
demands: Object to the Archdiocese honoring a donor to abortion access organizations
response: According to sources, Cardinal Blase Cupich defended the award, stating it recognizes community leadership and generosity without implying an endorsement of every stance held by the recipient.

updates.text: Illinois Right to Life held a public protest outside the Rerum Novarum Banquet objecting to the award recipient.
